jobs.location: Fort St John, British Columbia, Canada
jobs.description:
Company Description

FLINT is a leading service provider in Canada’s energy and industrial markets offering full asset life cycle support, including construction, maintenance, fabrication, and environmental services. Committed to safety and quality, we foster a workplace culture that values innovation and sustainability. With a strong local presence and top-tier talent, we deliver high-quality services as we help our customers bring their resources to our world.

Job Description

This position will be based out of our Fort St. John, BC office.

As an Environmental Professional at FLINT, you will support a variety of environmental projects, providing technical expertise in environmental assessments, regulatory compliance, and remediation activities. In this dynamic position, you'll lead various environmental field programs focused on-site investigations, remediation, and reclamation, all while championing a client-centered approach that drives success and fosters growth.

What would you be doing?

Perform site investigations, remediation, and reclamation activities including borehole logging, soil sampling, and supervising third-party contractors in compliance with regulatory standards.
Conduct technical analyses including hydraulic conductivity testing and groundwater flow calculations, while preparing reports and managing groundwater monitoring programs.
Foster strong relationships with suppliers, landowners, stakeholders, and regulators to enhance project outcomes and facilitate effective collaboration.
Crosstrain to adapt to seasonal demands and support other environmental projects as needed.
Spend up to 80% of time in the field, actively involved in hands-on environmental work across various practice areas.

Perks of the job

Competitive compensation.
Health coverage for you and your family.
RRSP matching.
Professional designation allowance.
Opportunity for internal development and growth.

Qualifications

Technical diploma or university degree in environmental science, engineering, or a related field; eligible for or holds a professional designation (e.g., Agrologist, Biologist, Engineer, Geoscientist).
1-3 years of experience in environmental consulting with hands-on expertise in fieldwork.
Proficient in safely operating light-duty trucks and holding a valid Class 5 driver's license.
Deep understanding and application of provincial environmental regulations, policies and guidelines pertinent to site investigations.
Skilled in planning and managing multiple projects under tight deadlines, ensuring continued stakeholder collaboration with a proactive approach to challenges and a commitment to health and safety standards.
Proficient in English, both written and verbal communication required.

Additional Information

This position has been identified as a safety-sensitive position and will require completion of drug and alcohol testing. 

Hourly Salary Range: $30.32 - $42.45

Your work will matter.The projects you'll help build will serve communities for generations.
Your growth is our priority.We'll invest in your development and create paths for advancement.
Your voice will be heard.Your experience and ideas will shape how we tackle challenges.
Your team will support you.You'll work with people who want to see you succeed.
Your ambition will be rewarded.As you grow, FLINT grows – and we recognize those who help us build better.

jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

When it comes to the most challenging environmental issues facing our communities today, we’re focused on developing and delivering the most innovative solutions to improve our tomorrow. We’re looking for a Mid-Level Environmental Engineer/Geologist/Scientist to continue their career at Jacobs – where we’ll empower you to learn and grow in the delivery of environmental site characterization and remediation projects for government and global private-sector clients to make our world better.

Based in Cincinnati, OH, you’ll participate in a variety of field and office tasks related to planning and implementing environmental investigation and remediation projects. You’ll learn from other experienced staff who are ready to mentor you, and you’ll pass your knowledge on to others. You’ll gain valuable experience in soil and groundwater sampling as well as drilling and subcontractor oversight, spending about 50% of your time in the field. You’ll balance your field work with some time spent in the office evaluating and reviewing data, writing reports and preparing project documents, and coordinating logistics for field activities. You’ll be juggling multiple tasks, so we’ll rely on you to prioritize effectively, keeping the big-picture in mind.

Here's What You'll Do

Lead and Manage Field Projects
Collaborate and Coordinate Work with subcontractors, internal support staff, and subject matter experts.
Technical Excellence Analyze data, prepare technical reports, and design and implement pilot studies and remedial systems.
Mentorship and Growth Provide motivation and direction to project teams, and benefit from mentorship opportunities to help you grow your career at Jacobs.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, geology, or other closely related degree
4+ years of professional experience with delivering environmental site characterization and remediation projects, including fieldwork methodology/procedures and assessment/evaluation of data for various environmental media.
Experience working on project sites and overseeing subcontractors
Experience leading teams toward a common goal.
40-hr HAZWOPER certification or the ability to attain this certification

Ideally, You’ll Also Have

Master’s degree in engineering, geology, or other closely related degree
Professional registration (e.g., Professional Engineer or Professional Geologist) or the intent to obtain and maintain professional certification.
Effective verbal and written communication skills with coworkers, contractors, and clients
Strong attention to detail when conducting field work and evaluating data.
Familiarity of United State Environmental Protection Agency regulations including CERCLA and RCRA

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $61,700.00 to $87,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on September 14, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

By joining Jacobs, you’ll commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Location: White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico

Title: Environmental Scientist

Schedule (FT/PT): Regular Full Time

Travel Required: No

Government Clearance: Ability to Obtain

North Wind Site Services is comprised of scientists and technical experts focused on providing program management and environmental remediation services including investigation and characterization, environmental restoration, remedial action, regulatory public involvement services, environmental compliance, logistics, and records and facility management.

Position Purpose

Support environmental regulatory compliance projects at White Sands Missile Range (WSMR), NM. The WSMR is regulated by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), New Mexico Environment Department (NMED), Federal Executive Orders, and WSMR environmental policy and guidelines. The position will be responsible for ensuring compliance with environmental Federal, State and WSMR regulations related to the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), and other environmental areas.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Ensure compliance with environmental regulations related to hazardous waste, universal waste and used oil.
Collaborate with environmental scientists, planners, hazardous waste technicians, engineers, and other specialists to address environmental problems.
Review waste characterization data and apply EPA hazardous waste identification codes.
Conduct sampling of various environmental media, assist with data interpretation and reporting.
Communicate scientific and regulatory information to clients, peers, and other site personnel through oral briefings, written documents, and formal meetings.
Participate in field efforts as needed to support the successful execution of projects.
Under the guidance of the Project Manager, evaluate analytical laboratory data and draw conclusions and make recommendations.
Prepare, review, and update technical reports.

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience:

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Science or related field; or technical training combined with 5 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrate knowledge of RCRA permit compliance and requirements.
Working knowledge of waste characterization and hazardous waste determinations per EPA regulations.
Working knowledge of waste management operations including labeling and documentation procedures.

Skills And Abilities

Demonstrated ability to work accurately, follow instructions/schedules/timelines and handle multiple priorities.
Excellent interpersonal skills; work effectively and cooperatively with all levels of management and staff, and client as well as outside business associates.
Strong oral and written communication skills; ability to effectively present information and respond effectively and sensitively to questions from client, managers, staff, and plant operational personnel.
Ability to work independently, as well as part of a team, and make decisions, solve problems, exercise good judgment, work under pressure, work with minimal supervision and prioritize workload.
Proficiency with MS Excel and Word
Commitment to health and safety in the workplace.

Special Requirements

Ability to pass Federal background check and pre-employment drug screening
Must have valid driver’s license

Preferred Qualifications

Current OSHA HAZWOPER certification is preferred.
Advanced Hazardous Waste Management Certification.
DoT HazMat ground shipper certification.
Working knowledge of hazardous waste management procedures.

Physical Demands

Ability to safely operate waste drum handling equipment such as forklifts, dollies, bung wrenches, etc.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods; safety operate motor vehicles in traffic and on unimproved roads.

Working Environment

Outdoors and indoors including warehouse environment.
Will include working under difficult conditions with extreme heat, humidity, and wind.
Will be exposed to moving parts/equipment, forklifts, lift gates, trucks, etc.

jobs.description:
STV is hiring a for a Florida Project Development & Environmental (PD&E) Director to drive the Transportation project lifecycle across Florida.

Locations: Tampa, Jacksonville, Orlando

You will join STV
, an award‑winning national leader consistently ranked among the country’s top firms in the design and planning of infrastructure and transportation systems. With more than 100 years of experience, STV delivers comprehensive architectural, engineering, planning, environmental, and construction management services to public and private sector clients nationwide.

You will step into a high‑growth Transportation & Infrastructure practice
with a strong backlog and significant opportunity across Central and North Florida. As STV continues to expand its PD&E capabilities statewide,
you will play a critical role in winning work, strengthening client relationships, and positioning the firm for downstream design and delivery opportunities
.

Why This Role Matters

This role is critical to STV’s long‑term growth strategy in Florida. Project Development & Environmental (PD&E) work is the front door to the transportation project lifecycle, positioning the firm to secure significant follow‑on design and Construction Engineering & Inspection (CEI) opportunities. With an established foundation already in place
, STV is seeking a seller‑doer
to re‑accelerate momentum, strengthen its competitive position, and lead PD&E pursuits across key FDOT districts
. Success in this role directly influences STV’s ability to win large, multi‑year programs
and expand its market presence across Florida, making this a highly visible, high‑impact opportunity with lasting influence on the firm’s future pipeline
.

How Success Is Measured

This is a visible leadership role for a proven seller‑doer
who thrives in front of clients, enjoys leading complex pursuits
, and builds teams that deliver. Success will be reflected in sustained PD&E wins, expanded client trust, and measurable growth
of STV’s transportation pipeline across priority FDOT districts.

What You’ll Be Doing

You will serve as a Project Development and Environmental (PD&E) Director
, helping shape STV’s PD&E strategy and presence across Florida. You will be a trusted client partner, a technical leader, and a practice builder -
equally comfortable leading pursuits, guiding teams, and delivering high‑profile PD&E projects
.

You will collaborate closely with senior leadership and transportation agencies
, drive growth in targeted FDOT districts, and help expand STV’s influence across the PD&E lifecycle, from early planning through environmental approval and into follow‑on design work.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

Building and growing STV’s PD&E practice across Florida, including staff development, mentoring, and succession planning.
Serving as a seller‑doer, leading client development, positioning, and pursuit strategy for PD&E and planning opportunities.
Acting as a senior client interface with FDOT and other transportation agencies at the federal, state, and local levels.
Leading the preparation and oversight of PD&E documents, including Preliminary Engineering Reports, alternatives analyses, feasibility studies, Type 1 & 2 CEs, EAs, and EISs.
Managing and directing multi‑disciplinary technical teams to deliver PD&E and planning projects.
Establishing and negotiating project scopes, budgets, staffing plans, schedules, and delivery strategies.
Partnering with other directors and practice leaders to ensure consistent technical standards and high‑quality execution.
Driving collaboration across planning, engineering, environmental, and traffic disciplines to achieve client outcomes
Strengthening and expanding key client relationships and converting those relationships into new work.
Supporting public involvement efforts, executive‑level briefings, and stakeholder presentations.
Representing STV through industry participation, thought leadership, and market visibility.

What You’ll Need To Succeed

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or Planning (Master’s degree preferred).
Minimum of 10 years of PD&E and NEPA experience, with demonstrated leadership on complex transportation programs.
Florida Professional Engineer (PE) license or AICP certification.
Direct experience delivering transportation planning and PD&E studies, including alternatives analyses, feasibility studies, and environmental documentation.
FDOT experience required, with strong familiarity across districts and agency processes.
A proven track record as a seller‑doer, including business development, client management, and winning work.
Experience leading and managing multi‑disciplinary teams on technically complex projects.
Strong professional reputation and market presence within Florida’s transportation community.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including client presentations and executive‑level discussions.
Proven project management and financial management capabilities.

Compensation Range

$184,970.12 - $205,522.35

STV offers the following benefits

Health insurance, including an option with a Health Savings Account
Dental insurance
Vision insurance
Flexible Spending Accounts (Healthcare, Dependent Care and Transit and Parking where applicable)
Disability insurance
Life Insurance and Accidental Death & Dismemberment
401(k) Plan
Retirement Counseling
Employee Assistance Program
Paid Time Off
Paid Holidays
Back-Up Dependent Care
Parental Leave
Continuing Education Program
Professional Licensure and Society Memberships

Please note that the final salary offered for this position may be outside of this published range based on many factors, including but not limited to geography, education, experience, and/or certifications.

jobs.description:
Department Information

The primary duties of this position are located within 30 miles of the state border; therefore, this position is exempt from the residency requirements. Applications will be considered from residents and non-residents of Colorado.

This is a term-limited position. Funding cannot be guaranteed beyond October, 2029. The incumbent in this position must be willing and able to resign on this date or when funds run out, whichever comes first.

Consider joining the dedicated people of the Colorado Department of Natural Resources. It’s our mission to manage and conserve Colorado’s natural resources for the benefit of people today – and tomorrow. That means we have to balance development with conservation so the state we all love provides similar opportunities for our children and their children.

We invite you to explore our website at https://dnr.colorado.gov/about-us to find out more about the work we do to manage Colorado’s natural resources for today – and tomorrow.

The State of Colorado believes that equity, diversity, and inclusion drive our success, and we encourage candidates from all identities, backgrounds, and abilities to apply.

In Addition To Offering Rewarding, Meaningful Work, We Offer

Medical and Dental plans
Strong, flexible retirement plans including PERA Defined Benefit Plan or PERA Defined Contribution Plan, plus pre-tax and Roth 401K and 457 plans
Paid life insurance
Short- and long-term disability coverage
Employee Wellness programs
Flexible Spending Accounts
Health Savings Accounts
11 paid holidays per year plus generous vacation and sick leave
Flexible work schedule options and remote-work options
Career advancement opportunities throughout the State system
Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program .

COLORADO PARKS AND WILDLIFE

Our Mission is to perpetuate the wildlife resources of the state, to provide a quality state parks system, and to provide enjoyable and sustainable outdoor recreation opportunities that educate and inspire current and future generations to serve as active stewards of Colorado's natural resources.

Wildlife Health conducts disease monitoring and surveillance for all terrestrial wildlife species, as well as rigorous scientific-based original research deemed valuable to CPW in order to better understand and enhance the health, management, and conservation of Colorado’s terrestrial wildlife resources; the program also provides field and laboratory services and training to CPW staff, as well as captive wildlife research support and captive wildlife holding for other CPW research and management programs.

Description Of Job

The position exists to: (a) provide technical support for necropsy services through statewide coordination of necropsy submissions, assistance during necropsy procedures, and maintenance of the necropsy laboratory; (b) provide technical support in executing statewide chronic wasting disease and other disease surveillance; (c) provide technical support for necropsy and laboratory services by maintaining records, filing paperwork, maintaining databases, and summarizing data (d) provide technical support for management or research projects conducted in the field or at the Foothills Wildlife Research Facility.

Provide technical support for necropsy services through coordination of necropsy submissions, assistance during necropsy procedures, and maintenance of the necropsy laboratory

Coordinate transportation of carcasses or tissues to the Wildlife Health Laboratory, including travel to retrieve carcasses when necessary. Coordinate sample submissions, and accession and process samples as they arrive at the Wildlife Health Laboratory. Adhere to protocols for ongoing disease surveillance projects. Maintain adequate facility and supplies/inventory for necropsy and other diagnostic services. Maintain clean and sanitary work, freezer, and cooler spaces, including timely disposition of tissues after processing either through disposal at a landfill or via incineration. Monitor freezers and coolers for adequate temperature control. Monitor hazardous waste tanks and coordinate disposal of hazardous material as needed. Provide support during necropsy including dissection, tissue removal, assessment of tissue integrity/disease, radiology, photography, proper sample handling for diagnostics or archival, and submission to external and internal laboratories for testing. Mail coolers back to submitters. Take personal responsibility for the use of personal protective equipment when dealing with potentially hazardous tissues or chemicals. Maintain archives of samples, photographs, reports, and other documents pertinent to casework. Special care must be taken for forensics cases that may provide evidence for legal investigations.

Provide technical support to the laboratory technologist in executing statewide chronic wasting disease and other disease surveillance

This position will also perform duties related to CWD surveillance and other disease surveillance. Duties may include, but are not limited to Construct and mail out supplies for CWD sampling (CWD kits). Provide training for CWD sampling. Process CWD samples as they arrive at the Wildlife Health Laboratory. Extract CWD samples from whole head submissions. Assure sample quality for submissions. Organize samples for submission to the diagnostic laboratory. Submit samples to the diagnostic laboratory. Enter data and provide quality control for data entries in the CWD database. Communicate with field personnel and other staff to assure quick resolution of any issues. Accession and process samples arriving at the lab for purposes other than CWD or necropsy (for example blood or tissue samples received from research staff). Properly archive samples in accordance with existing protocols.

Provide technical support for necropsy and laboratory services by maintaining records, filing paperwork, maintaining databases, and summarizing data

This position will manage paperwork from necropsy and sample submissions to the wildlife health laboratory and develop mechanisms to organize and track diagnostic data.

Provide technical support for management or research projects conducted in the field or at the Foothills
Wildlife Research Facility.

Assist veterinary staff, researchers, managers, and biologists with ongoing projects including animal care and husbandry, observation, veterinary care and support, sample collection and handling, data collection, or other duties to support this work. Travel may be required.

Other Duties As Assigned.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

Minimum Qualifications

Four (4) years of relevant experience in wildlife health, processing biological samples, post-mortem tissue handling and sampling or an occupational field related to the work assigned to the position. You must adequately demonstrate your experience in your application as it relates to the duties of this position.

OR

A combination of related education in wildlife biology, natural resources, animal science, biology and/or relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned equal to four (4) years.

Substitutions

Appropriate education in wildlife biology, natural resources, animal science, biology, laboratory science or a related field of study will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.

You must adequately demonstrate your experience in your application as it relates to the duties of this position.

Class Code:
TECHNICIAN IV

Preferred Qualifications

Current or former Colorado Parks & Wildlife work or volunteer experience is considered.
Experience collecting and processing a wide array of biological samples.
Experience managing detailed records and quality control of data.
Experience working with strong smells and decaying tissues with varying amounts of maggots or other insects.
Experience collecting post mortem samples.
Current or former State experience relevant to this position.

Required Competencies

Excellent organizational and time management skills.
Strong level of written and oral communication skills.
Ability to use and operate computers and email and basic data management (e.g., Excel, Access).
Ability to strictly follow laboratory protocols and procedures.
Ability to move smoothly between highly variable tasks.
Attention to detail and quality assurance during sample processing.

Conditions of Employment

Will be required to operate a State vehicle. Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license.
Occasional assistance with field work may require travel.
Must willing and able to obtain record of rabies vaccine for consideration of employment.
Employee will be exposed to biological materials as well as formalin, a hazardous chemical must be fit for a respirator (such as an N95 face mask) as they will be exposed to animal carcasses positive for infectious diseases such as rabies, highly pathogenic avian influenza, plague, and tularemia PPE during necropsy activities.
Employee must be capable of lifting up to 50 pounds and performing varied physical tasks such as bending, crouching, lifting, and reaching.
Former State employees who were disciplinarily terminated or resigned in lieu of termination must disclose the information on the application and provide an explanation why the prior termination or resignation should not disqualify their application from the current position. (Please Note: Absent extraordinary circumstances, prior disciplinary termination or resignation in lieu of termination will disqualify the applicant from future State employment with DNR).
Pursuant to the DNR-120 Fleet and Driving Standards Administrative Directive , any worker who will be expected to drive a State-owned vehicle is responsible for maintaining a safe driving record and a valid driver license prior to driving any State-owned vehicle.

To Be Compliant With The New Fleet Vehicle Policy, Motor Vehicle Records (MVRs) Will Be Pulled For Review For Workers Who

Have an assigned State fleet vehicle
Are required to operate a vehicle as part of the position
Utilize a State fleet vehicle as a pool vehicle

Appeal Rights

It is recommended that you contact the Human Resources Specialist listed below to resolve issues related to your possession of minimum qualifications. However, if you receive notice that you have been eliminated from consideration for this position, you may file an appeal with the State Personnel Board or request a review by the State Personnel Director.

An appeal or review must be submitted on the official appeal form, signed by you or your representative. This form must be delivered to the State Personnel Board by email (dpa_state.personnelboard@state.co.us), postmarked in US Mail or hand delivered (1525 Sherman Street, 4th Floor, Denver CO 80203), or faxed (303.866.5038) within ten (10) calendar days from your receipt of notice or acknowledgment of the department’s action.

For more information about the appeals process, the official appeal form, and how to deliver it to the State Personnel Board; go to spb.colorado.gov; contact the State Personnel Board for assistance at (303) 866-3300; or refer to 4 Colorado Code of Regulations (CCR) 801-1, State Personnel Board Rules and Personnel Director's Administrative Procedures, Chapter 8, Resolution of Appeals and Disputes, at spb.colorado.gov under Rules.

The Assessment Process

Reviews air quality applications from assigned facilities for State Construction Permits; State Construction Approvals; Class I Operating Permits and Class II Operating Permits. Applications are reviewed to ensure compliance with provisions of the Clean Air Act, including National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), New Source Performance Standards (NSPS), National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAPs), and State of Kansas air quality regulations. STV is hiring a for a Florida Project Development & Environmental (PD&E) Director to drive the Transportation project lifecycle across Florida.

You will join STV
, an award‑winning national leader consistently ranked among the country’s top firms in the design and planning of infrastructure and transportation systems. You will step into a high‑growth Transportation & Infrastructure practice

.

. Success in this role directly influences STV’s ability to win large, multi‑year programs
and expand its market presence across Florida, making this a highly visible, high‑impact opportunity with lasting influence on the firm’s future pipeline
.

This is a visible leadership role for a proven seller‑doer

, and builds teams that deliver. Success will be reflected in sustained PD&E wins, expanded client trust, and measurable growth
of STV’s transportation pipeline across priority FDOT districts.

, helping shape STV’s PD&E strategy and presence across Florida. You will be a trusted client partner, a technical leader, and a practice builder -

.

, drive growth in targeted FDOT districts, and help expand STV’s influence across the PD&E lifecycle, from early planning through environmental approval and into follow‑on design work.

Partnering with other directors and practice leaders to ensure consistent technical standards and high‑quality execution.
Driving collaboration across planning, engineering, environmental, and traffic disciplines to achieve client outcomes
Strengthening and expanding key client relationships and converting those relationships into new work.
Supporting public involvement efforts, executive‑level briefings, and stakeholder presentations.
Representing STV through industry participation, thought leadership, and market visibility.

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or Planning (Master’s degree preferred).
Minimum of 10 years of PD&E and NEPA experience, with demonstrated leadership on complex transportation programs.
Florida Professional Engineer (PE) license or AICP certification.
Direct experience delivering transportation planning and PD&E studies, including alternatives analyses, feasibility studies, and environmental documentation.
FDOT experience required, with strong familiarity across districts and agency processes.
A proven track record as a seller‑doer, including business development, client management, and winning work.
Experience leading and managing multi‑disciplinary teams on technically complex projects.
Strong professional reputation and market presence within Florida’s transportation community.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including client presentations and executive‑level discussions.
Proven project management and financial management capabilities.

$184,970.12 - $205,522.35

401(k) Plan
Retirement Counseling
Employee Assistance Program
Paid Time Off
Paid Holidays

Parental Leave
Continuing Education Program
Professional Licensure and Society Memberships

Consider joining the dedicated people of the Colorado Department of Natural Resources. It’s our mission to manage and conserve Colorado’s natural resources for the benefit of people today – and tomorrow. That means we have to balance development with conservation so the state we all love provides similar opportunities for our children and their children.

We invite you to explore our website at https://dnr.colorado.gov/about-us to find out more about the work we do to manage Colorado’s natural resources for today – and tomorrow.

Medical and Dental plans

Short- and long-term disability coverage

11 paid holidays per year plus generous vacation and sick leave

Career advancement opportunities throughout the State system

COLORADO PARKS AND WILDLIFE

Our Mission is to perpetuate the wildlife resources of the state, to provide a quality state parks system, and to provide enjoyable and sustainable outdoor recreation opportunities that educate and inspire current and future generations to serve as active stewards of Colorado's natural resources.

Wildlife Health conducts disease monitoring and surveillance for all terrestrial wildlife species, as well as rigorous scientific-based original research deemed valuable to CPW in order to better understand and enhance the health, management, and conservation of Colorado’s terrestrial wildlife resources; the program also provides field and laboratory services and training to CPW staff, as well as captive wildlife research support and captive wildlife holding for other CPW research and management programs.

Description Of Job

The position exists to: (a) provide technical support for necropsy services through statewide coordination of necropsy submissions, assistance during necropsy procedures, and maintenance of the necropsy laboratory; (b) provide technical support in executing statewide chronic wasting disease and other disease surveillance; (c) provide technical support for necropsy and laboratory services by maintaining records, filing paperwork, maintaining databases, and summarizing data (d) provide technical support for management or research projects conducted in the field or at the Foothills Wildlife Research Facility.

Provide technical support for necropsy services through coordination of necropsy submissions, assistance during necropsy procedures, and maintenance of the necropsy laboratory

Coordinate transportation of carcasses or tissues to the Wildlife Health Laboratory, including travel to retrieve carcasses when necessary. Coordinate sample submissions, and accession and process samples as they arrive at the Wildlife Health Laboratory. Adhere to protocols for ongoing disease surveillance projects. Maintain adequate facility and supplies/inventory for necropsy and other diagnostic services. Maintain clean and sanitary work, freezer, and cooler spaces, including timely disposition of tissues after processing either through disposal at a landfill or via incineration. Monitor freezers and coolers for adequate temperature control. Monitor hazardous waste tanks and coordinate disposal of hazardous material as needed. Provide support during necropsy including dissection, tissue removal, assessment of tissue integrity/disease, radiology, photography, proper sample handling for diagnostics or archival, and submission to external and internal laboratories for testing. Mail coolers back to submitters. Take personal responsibility for the use of personal protective equipment when dealing with potentially hazardous tissues or chemicals. Maintain archives of samples, photographs, reports, and other documents pertinent to casework. Special care must be taken for forensics cases that may provide evidence for legal investigations.

Provide technical support to the laboratory technologist in executing statewide chronic wasting disease and other disease surveillance

This position will also perform duties related to CWD surveillance and other disease surveillance. Duties may include, but are not limited to Construct and mail out supplies for CWD sampling (CWD kits). Provide training for CWD sampling. Process CWD samples as they arrive at the Wildlife Health Laboratory. Extract CWD samples from whole head submissions. Assure sample quality for submissions. Organize samples for submission to the diagnostic laboratory. Submit samples to the diagnostic laboratory. Enter data and provide quality control for data entries in the CWD database. Communicate with field personnel and other staff to assure quick resolution of any issues. Accession and process samples arriving at the lab for purposes other than CWD or necropsy (for example blood or tissue samples received from research staff). Properly archive samples in accordance with existing protocols.

Provide technical support for necropsy and laboratory services by maintaining records, filing paperwork, maintaining databases, and summarizing data

This position will manage paperwork from necropsy and sample submissions to the wildlife health laboratory and develop mechanisms to organize and track diagnostic data.

Provide technical support for management or research projects conducted in the field or at the Foothills
Wildlife Research Facility.

Assist veterinary staff, researchers, managers, and biologists with ongoing projects including animal care and husbandry, observation, veterinary care and support, sample collection and handling, data collection, or other duties to support this work. Travel may be required.

Other Duties As Assigned.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

Minimum Qualifications

Four (4) years of relevant experience in wildlife health, processing biological samples, post-mortem tissue handling and sampling or an occupational field related to the work assigned to the position. You must adequately demonstrate your experience in your application as it relates to the duties of this position.

OR

A combination of related education in wildlife biology, natural resources, animal science, biology and/or relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned equal to four (4) years.

Substitutions

Appropriate education in wildlife biology, natural resources, animal science, biology, laboratory science or a related field of study will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.

You must adequately demonstrate your experience in your application as it relates to the duties of this position.

Class Code:
TECHNICIAN IV

Preferred Qualifications

Current or former Colorado Parks & Wildlife work or volunteer experience is considered.
Experience collecting and processing a wide array of biological samples.
Experience managing detailed records and quality control of data.
Experience working with strong smells and decaying tissues with varying amounts of maggots or other insects.
Experience collecting post mortem samples.
Current or former State experience relevant to this position.

Required Competencies

Excellent organizational and time management skills.
Strong level of written and oral communication skills.
Ability to use and operate computers and email and basic data management (e.g., Excel, Access).
Ability to strictly follow laboratory protocols and procedures.
Ability to move smoothly between highly variable tasks.
Attention to detail and quality assurance during sample processing.

Conditions of Employment

Employee will be exposed to biological materials as well as formalin, a hazardous chemical must be fit for a respirator (such as an N95 face mask) as they will be exposed to animal carcasses positive for infectious diseases such as rabies, highly pathogenic avian influenza, plague, and tularemia PPE during necropsy activities.

STV is hiring a for a Florida Project Development & Environmental (PD&E) Director to drive the Transportation project lifecycle across Florida.

Locations: Tampa, Jacksonville, Orlando

You will join STV
, an award‑winning national leader consistently ranked among the country’s top firms in the design and planning of infrastructure and transportation systems. With more than 100 years of experience, STV delivers comprehensive architectural, engineering, planning, environmental, and construction management services to public and private sector clients nationwide.

You will step into a high‑growth Transportation & Infrastructure practice
with a strong backlog and significant opportunity across Central and North Florida. As STV continues to expand its PD&E capabilities statewide,
you will play a critical role in winning work, strengthening client relationships, and positioning the firm for downstream design and delivery opportunities
.

This role is critical to STV’s long‑term growth strategy in Florida. Project Development & Environmental (PD&E) work is the front door to the transportation project lifecycle, positioning the firm to secure significant follow‑on design and Construction Engineering & Inspection (CEI) opportunities. With an established foundation already in place

to re‑accelerate momentum, strengthen its competitive position, and lead PD&E pursuits across key FDOT districts
. Success in this role directly influences STV’s ability to win large, multi‑year programs
and expand its market presence across Florida, making this a highly visible, high‑impact opportunity with lasting influence on the firm’s future pipeline
.

How Success Is Measured

This is a visible leadership role for a proven seller‑doer
who thrives in front of clients, enjoys leading complex pursuits
, and builds teams that deliver. Success will be reflected in sustained PD&E wins, expanded client trust, and measurable growth
of STV’s transportation pipeline across priority FDOT districts.

What You’ll Be Doing

You will serve as a Project Development and Environmental (PD&E) Director
, helping shape STV’s PD&E strategy and presence across Florida. You will be a trusted client partner, a technical leader, and a practice builder -
equally comfortable leading pursuits, guiding teams, and delivering high‑profile PD&E projects
.

You will collaborate closely with senior leadership and transportation agencies
, drive growth in targeted FDOT districts, and help expand STV’s influence across the PD&E lifecycle, from early planning through environmental approval and into follow‑on design work.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

Building and growing STV’s PD&E practice across Florida, including staff development, mentoring, and succession planning.
Serving as a seller‑doer, leading client development, positioning, and pursuit strategy for PD&E and planning opportunities.
Acting as a senior client interface with FDOT and other transportation agencies at the federal, state, and local levels.

Managing and directing multi‑disciplinary technical teams to deliver PD&E and planning projects.
Establishing and negotiating project scopes, budgets, staffing plans, schedules, and delivery strategies.
Partnering with other directors and practice leaders to ensure consistent technical standards and high‑quality execution.
Driving collaboration across planning, engineering, environmental, and traffic disciplines to achieve client outcomes
Strengthening and expanding key client relationships and converting those relationships into new work.
Supporting public involvement efforts, executive‑level briefings, and stakeholder presentations.
Representing STV through industry participation, thought leadership, and market visibility.

What You’ll Need To Succeed

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or Planning (Master’s degree preferred).
Minimum of 10 years of PD&E and NEPA experience, with demonstrated leadership on complex transportation programs.
Florida Professional Engineer (PE) license or AICP certification.
Direct experience delivering transportation planning and PD&E studies, including alternatives analyses, feasibility studies, and environmental documentation.
FDOT experience required, with strong familiarity across districts and agency processes.
A proven track record as a seller‑doer, including business development, client management, and winning work.
Experience leading and managing multi‑disciplinary teams on technically complex projects.
Strong professional reputation and market presence within Florida’s transportation community.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including client presentations and executive‑level discussions.
Proven project management and financial management capabilities.

Position Summary & Responsibilities

Position Summary:
Position (K0229186)

The Bureau of Air, Permitting Unit, is seeking a candidate for an Environmental Specialist position. Responsibilities include review of construction and operating permit applications, source information, air emission calculations, and other documents provided by permit applicants for compliance with the Clean Air Act federal regulations and Kansas Air Quality Regulations.

Job Responsibilities may include but are not limited to the following:

Reviews air quality applications from assigned facilities for State Construction Permits; State Construction Approvals; Class I Operating Permits and Class II Operating Permits. Applications are reviewed to ensure compliance with provisions of the Clean Air Act, including National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), New Source Performance Standards (NSPS), National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAPs), and State of Kansas air quality regulations. Applications are reviewed to ensure all necessary air quality information is provided by permit applicant. Incumbent reviews technical air quality reports, environmental plans and specifications for the construction or modification of air pollution control facilities to determine if facility designers have made accurate and appropriate conclusions in their preparation of air permit applications. Air quality permit applications emission calculations are analyzed to ensure compliance with sound engineering practices and established air quality standards. Analysis of air quality control technology to reduce emissions and ensure compliance with environmental regulations in air permits is performed. Incumbent directly contacts environmental and engineering consultants, planners, and designers to resolve any questions. Verifies that all air quality regulations in permit applications are appropriate for the type and class of permit requested.

Develop permits including Class I and Class II Operating permits and Construction permits. Review must ensure that emissions from both new construction and modifications do not cause or contribute to violations of the NAAQS and assure new construction and modifications will comply with all applicable air quality regulations. Operating Permits consist in the development of a single document which contains all air quality requirements with which the source must comply. Permits are developed to ensure adherence to all federal and State regulations and Bureau of Air policies and procedures. Once a draft permit has been completed and gone through an internal concurrence process, the permit is issued to the applicant. All construction approvals, construction permits, and operating permits are reviewed by supervisor and section chief. All reviews occur at the time a draft permit has been submitted for concurrence.

Assured that all statutory, regulatory, contractual and procedural requirements have been satisfied prior to issuance of a permit, including notifications to EPA required by agreement with the EPA. This final step in the issuance of less complex and routine permits is to ensure that EPA air permit requirements have been met by verifying compliance with all aspects of the Clean Air Act, as indicated by the state's air pollution control strategies listed in the State implementation Plan submitted to EPA. These requirements are usually reviewed during the internal concurrence process; however, EPA does review and comment on some of these permits, in addition to auditing the Bureau of Air's permit program. During the permit concurrence process, work is reviewed by supervisor and section chief for compliance with Kansas Air Quality Act, related regulations and federal Clean Air Act requirements.
